explanation: ἀνδροτῆτα must scan ∪ ∪ – ∪, i.e. ἀν- short before νδρ; no rule of position allows this. Monro, Homeric Grammar §370 (end) suggests reading ἀδροτῆτα. Not fixed: a rule that lets a vowel stay short before νδρ would be ad hoc and would only serve these three lines.
evidence: concordance --loose ανδροτητ: 3 lines, all fail the same way

explanation: The text has εὐστεφάνου (diphthong, 3 syllables); the metre needs ἐϋστεφάνου (4 syllables), the spelling the same edition uses in the same phrase at Od. 8.288 (φιλότητος ἐυστεφάνου Κυθερείης). The Greek is not edited.
evidence: concordance --loose στεφαν: Od. 8.288, Od. 18.193, Il. 19.99 have ἐϋ-/ἐυ-

explanation: The text has θείμεν (2 syllables) at verse start, where the metre needs a dactyl; Homer elsewhere has θείομεν in this place (Il. 1.143, 23.244). The Greek is not edited.
